title: stackfile
description: What a project builds with, how to use it, what to avoid, and which decisions back each choice. Written for people and coding agents.

stackfile.description: Format version. Also how tools tell this file apart from other YAML.

description.description: One or two sentences on what the project is.

principles.description: Tie-breakers for any choice this file does not cover yet.

layers.description: Entries grouped by layer. Layer names are free-form: backend, data, frontend, infra, testing, tooling.

avoid.description: Things not to introduce at all, with what to use instead.

rule.description: One short imperative sentence. Anything longer belongs in a docs page.

commands.description: Named shell commands: test, lint, migrate, dev.

ecosystem.description: The package manager that installs this, so it can be checked against a manifest.

basis.description: declared: stated, with no decision record behind it yet. pending: chosen in a record that is not accepted yet, named in pending_on. ratified: backed by the accepted records in decided_by. All three are binding. Basis covers the choice; a version is declared unless version_decided_by says otherwise.

decided_by.description: Identifiers of the accepted ADRs or RFCs that back this entry, such as ADR-0012.

pending_on.description: Identifiers of the records, not yet accepted, that will decide this entry, such as a draft RFC-0005.

name.description: Unique across the whole file. Other entries refer to it by this name.

version.description: A version constraint. Always a string: an unquoted 1.10 is the number 1.1.

version_decided_by.description: The accepted records that set the version, when they did. Without it the version is declared, whatever the entry's basis.

package.description: The package's name in its ecosystem, such as laravel/framework.

status.description: adopt: the default choice. trial: allowed within its scope while being evaluated. proposed: not decided, see candidates. hold: no new uses. retired: being removed, see replaced_by.

why.description: The reason in a sentence or two, until a decision record carries the full argument.

scope.description: Path globs, relative to this file, where the entry applies. Absent means everywhere.

docs.description: Path or URL to the longer explanation.

replaced_by.description: The name of the entry that replaces this one.

candidates.description: The options being considered while status is proposed. One is fine; so is none, when open states the question.

open.description: The question that has to be answered to decide.

use_instead.description: What to use in its place. An entry name, or plain words such as native fetch.
